⚠️ While doing it, the implementing dev found and **deliberately did not touch** a second sentence in the same file:

> Declaring `nodes` also does not by itself make a `nodes`-only tree-view document legal: `data` stays required on both faces.

Its report states this is **already false at that branch's base** — objectui#6939 made `nodes` optional and objectui#6951 retired `data` outright on both faces — and that it is ⛔ **not** falsified by anything on that branch.

⭐ Not touching it was the right call and the reason is worth keeping: the instruction was to correct the sentence that head falsifies and to rewrite nothing else. A dev widening a changeset edit on its own initiative is how a bounded correction turns into an unreviewable one. It reported instead.

### Why this is on your card rather than filed

The file is **yours**, it is **pending**, and it **publishes verbatim in the next release** — so a user would read a sentence about `data` and `nodes` that the code stopped honouring two cards ago.

⛔ This seat is not amending it: the sentence is untouched by any work this lane has in flight, so editing it here would be exactly the unbounded edit described above. ⇒ recorded for whoever holds this card, with two options and no recommendation:

1. Amend the sentence on this card, in its own change, before the release takes it.
2. Establish that it is **not** in fact false — the dev's reading of objectui#6939 / objectui#6951 is a **dated reading it took in passing**, ⛔ not a measurement this seat re-derived. If it is wrong, nothing is owed.

⚠️ ⛔ **Do not take option 2 on this comment's word.** Re-derive it against `origin/main`, because this whole thread of work exists because artefacts asserted things nobody had re-read.
